work.title: Readela 0.3.0: the release — a correction to the privacy wording, integration of pull request 9, the packages of the frozen commit, the tag and the release, and publication on Firefox Add-ons
work.ownerAuthorization: Owner instruction of 2026-10-13 for the release, and the sections of that day in DEC-143, ENT-243 and ENT-246 that record it. The owner approved the final 0.3.0 extension and popup, the five store screenshots and the public positioning. It authorizes: correcting privacy wording that could be read as a statement about the two sites rather than about the extension; marking pull request 9 ready and merging it into main once the integration Gate passes; building the packages and the source archive from the frozen commit on main; a v0.3.0 tag and a release on that commit; submitting version 0.3.0 to the existing Firefox add-on readela (readela@amir42.com), which publishes it, once the publication Gate passes; bringing that add-on's product page (summary, description, privacy policy, screenshots and captions) to 0.3.0 after the version is public; and a hand-off for the Chrome Web Store. It does not authorize: a change of what the extension does, requests, reads or stores, of its fonts, its features or its version number; an upload, a submission or any change of the live listing on the Chrome Web Store; a new store entry; entering credentials, accepting an agreement or completing a verification on the owner's behalf; or a write to Personal OS.

parentPreflight.reason: That record, and the full records for the code (ent-240-readela-0.3.0-reading-comfort.json, ent-246-readela-0.3.0-correction-5.json and the three popup records), place merging, the tag, the release and every submission out of scope. The release is that work, separately bounded and separately authorized, so it carries its own assertion, as the 0.2.1 release did. Those records stay the records for what they cover and are not edited; the integration Gate they left not yet evaluated is evaluated under this one.

inScope: This record, committed first on the existing branch from baseCommit.

docs/privacy-policy.md, docs/store-listing.md, README.md and docs/privacy-and-permissions.md: sentences about what is transmitted, reworded so that they speak of the extension and say that the two sites keep communicating with their own servers. No statement of fact about the extension changes.
Dated evidence under docs/evidence/, an accurate description of pull request 9, marking it ready and merging it into main with the repository's merge method.

From the frozen commit on main, in clean clones: the Chrome and Firefox packages, the source archive, their digests, a comparison with the candidate packages, and the checks of the release (verifier, unit tests, package contents, Mozilla's linter).
An annotated tag v0.3.0 on the frozen commit and a release that carries the three archives and their digests.

Firefox Add-ons, the existing add-on readela: a new version from the frozen Firefox package with the source archive, release notes and notes to the reviewer; after the version is public, the product page from docs/store-listing.md.
A hand-off for the owner's manual update of the Chrome Web Store item, and evidence kept outside the repository under the project's evidence convention.
outOfScope: Everything that is packaged: what runs in a page, the popup, the background component, the manifest, the commands, permissions, match patterns, web-accessible resources, stored forms, the fonts, the icons, and the version number.
The store images and the approved positioning of the copy, other than the privacy sentences named above.
The Chrome Web Store: no upload, no submission, no change of the listing or of a privacy field.
A new add-on or store entry, Firefox for Android, a new feature, a dependency change, a new build, packaging or release process.
A repeat of the hour-long memory comparison, unless this work shows a regression that calls for it.
Credentials, agreements and verifications of a provider, which stay the owner's.
Changes to declared Capabilities or Exceptions, to the dev-standards pin and to the repository ruleset, and any write to Personal OS.

risk.note: A published store version can only be superseded, so the exact-artifact discipline of the earlier releases is kept: every submitted file is built from one frozen commit on main and bound to it by SHA-256, the publication Gate names the artifact it assessed, and the product page is changed only after the version it describes is public.

A statement about privacy or permissions can be made true only by changing the extension.
The packages of the frozen commit differ from the candidate packages in a packaged file that this work does not explain.
The provider asks for something the authorization does not cover: a credential, an agreement, a verification, a new permission prompt for readers or a change of the add-on's identity.
Declared Capabilities or Exceptions change, or the applicable baseline identity changes.
HEAD stops descending from baseCommit before the merge.
